That means if you are within 27 feet of the bomb detonating, the blast wave alone has a chance to outright kill you (disregard shrapnel). Outside of that area lung damage threshold (30 psi) and eardrums rupture (15 psi, 50% probability) will occur at 38 and 53 feet respectively (per Unified Facilities Code 3-340-02).

To put this into perspective, the Trinity Test was approximately 5 to 10 kilotons (4500x weaker) while Little Boy was approximately 15kt (3000x weaker) and Fatman was approximately 21 kt (2000x weaker). Some more perspective, the eruption of Krakatoa is estimate at 200 megatons and Mount Saint Helen's eruption is estimated at 400 megatons (10x stronger).

My girlfriend is obsessed with knitting, what should I giver her as a gift?
Hey @NeedleStack, I need some gift advice

I'm thinking yarn and some new needles and stitch markers is the way to go. Our obsession and love of yarn is almost perverse.

But first I'll need some details. :)

Does she make scarves and hats or is she more advanced and is making sweaters and jackets?

Does she ever make socks or mittens/gloves or shawls?

Knowing what kinds of things she makes will help determine the size of the yarn you should give her. Thicker yarn (like worsted, aran, tweed, buiky, chunky) is good for hats, sweaters, jackets, blankets, etc. If she knits socks and shawls she'll like thinner yarns like lace-weight, fingering, sport, and dk yarns.

Does she have many sets of needles or just a couple? Are they straight? Does she have circular ones? Does she have knitting tools like stitch markers and needle point protectors and guage guides and tapestry needles? You may need to investigate further on this one.

I ask because it's always nice to get yarn and some nice tools like new stitch markers. If she doesn't have circular needles yet or just has one or two pairs, I highly recommend a set of circular needles. Get Hiya Hiya interchangeable needles. They're a bit pricey but will last pretty much forever. You can find sellers on Amazon and eBay. If she knits with thinner yarn most of the time, get her the smaller-sized needles (2-8). If she usually makes the bulkier items likes hats, scarves, and blankets get the larger-sized needles (9-15).

I need to know about the quality of yarn she uses. Can you find out if she has mostly acrylics? Wools? Silks? In any case, I think it would be great to splurge and get her some high quality yarns like pure (or blends of) hand-dyed silk, mohair, merino wool, etc. Since you need lots of yarn for a project, get her at least 2 balls/skeins of whatever yarn you get her. That way she won't be forced to make just a scarf and hat.

I hope this helps! If you get her stuff I hope you'll sneak us some photos of the goods. :)

She enjoys making things like patterned blankets, socks, fingerless gloves, and has recently started making sweaters. I personally don't pay attention to specifics, but I'm pretty sure she uses acrylic yarn.
The Hiya Hiya needles look cool, however they aren't really in my price range.

Hopefully this clarifies some. I might be able to sneak you some picture :)

Since she may be using acrylic I think she'll love some wool or a blend of mohair or alpaca or silk. You can find beautiful skeins of hand-dyed wool that will be perfect. Sort out what you think her favorite color might be for garments and look for types like "aran", "worsted", "DK/Double Knit", or "sport weight" yarn. They'll be the right sizes for her projects. :)
You're welcome! Good luck and let us know how it goes. :)
